description: The warehouse wants handheld NIR for identity testing of incoming excipients and media powders. The vendor's classification model was trained on our reference spectra and is locked; a pass releases the container for dispensing without any further ID test.
rationale: Identity testing that releases material for use directly affects product quality; a locked trained classifier is in A22 §1 scope and needs SME-approved acceptance criteria (§4.2) and configuration control (§10.2).

description: IT wants a chatbot on the intranet that answers questions about laptop setup, VPN, Outlook and printers, and opens a ticket when it can't help.
rationale: Generic office IT support is not a GMP activity; the AI Act transparency duty for systems interacting with people (Art. 50) is the relevant point.

description: Could an AI agent go through the executed electronic batch records, check them against the master record and the open deviations, and sign off the production review step itself so batches reach QP certification faster?
rationale: Batch record review before release is a GMP decision (FDA-WL cites failure to review batch records before release); A22 §1 excludes LLMs and agents from critical GMP applications.

description: Our CDS vendor offers an 'AI-assisted' peak integration add-on for the QC HPLC and CE methods. It integrates the peaks automatically and the analyst then reviews the integration as usual before results are reported. The vendor won't tell us how it works under the hood.
rationale: Peak integration determines reported QC results (critical), but whether the add-on is a trained model (Annex 22) or a classical algorithm (Annex 11) is unknown; A22 §2.2 expects supplier documentation to be available and reviewed, so this must be resolved first.

description: For new client tech transfers, MSAT wants an LLM to compare the client's process description and equipment list with our facility and draft the gap assessment. The engineers then go through it line by line and finalise it in the tech transfer protocol.
rationale: The draft supports a tech transfer document that engineers review and finalise, a non-critical use with qualified people responsible for the output (A22 §1).

description: QC lab planning tool that suggests the daily order of test runs and analyst assignments; it learns on its own every week from actual turnaround times. The lab supervisor adjusts and publishes the plan.
rationale: Scheduling is planning support (FDA-DP area 3 names scheduling) with no direct quality impact; A22 §1 excludes dynamic models only from critical uses, so risk-based controls apply.

description: Our eQMS has a 'smart triage' feature that assigns new deviations and change requests to the right department and owner based on keywords and the drop-down values entered. It's rules configured in the tool, and the assignment happens automatically.
rationale: Keyword and field rules are explicitly programmed configuration, not a trained model (A22 §1), so Annex 11 applies, including documented configuration (A11D 6.6).

description: We'd like a chatbot on our client portal that answers sponsors' questions about where their batches are, expected release dates and CoA results, pulling from SAP and LIMS. Answers would go out directly, 24/7.
rationale: It passes GMP information (batch status, CoA results) to clients without anyone checking the answers, so A22 §1's HITL expectation for LLMs in non-critical uses is not met; AI Act Art. 50 transparency also applies.

description: Can you summarise what changed between ICH Q9 and Q9(R1)?
Help me write my end-of-year self-assessment for my manager.
